summary.text: 还 is the simplified form of 還, whose documented sense includes “return; go back.” In later forms, 還 combines 辵, associated with movement, and 瞏, identified as a sound element. Modern 还 also means “still” and “yet,” but their development from “return” is not established.

formation.text: The later construction of 還 is phonosemantic: 辵 contributes a movement-related meaning and 瞏 is identified as the sound element. One analysis also proposes a meaning contribution from 瞏’s “round jade disc” sense; the received dictionary analysis assigns it only a sound role. The reported early forms have different analyses, and their relationship to this later construction is unresolved.

components.text: In 还, 辶 is the conventional side form of 辵. In later forms of 還, 辵 is associated with movement; this analysis does not apply to every reported early form.

不 is visible in modern 还, but its presence does not establish a meaning or sound role in the older construction of 還. A separate dictionary entry records a graph 还 associated with 不 but does not connect it to this variant.

In later forms of 還, 瞏 is identified as a sound element. One reported Old Chinese comparison pairs 還 *ɡʷraːn with 睘 *ɡʷeŋ, but does not independently verify the component’s identity or the sound fit. Another analysis proposes that 瞏’s “round jade disc” sense contributes meaning; the received analysis assigns it only a sound role.

sound_limitation.text: The reported comparison does not independently establish that 睘 is the component intended in 還 or verify the proposed sound fit.

sound.text: A reported Old Chinese comparison pairs 還 *ɡʷraːn with 睘 *ɡʷeŋ; it proposes a historical sound relationship but does not independently verify the fit.

history.text: Reported early forms of 還 have differing analyses: some oracle-bone forms are analyzed as 行/目/方, while a separate Zhouyuan form is described as 彳/睘. Later bronze and seal forms are analyzed with 辵 and 睘. These descriptions do not establish a continuous graphic transition.

The received dictionary analysis writes 還 as 从辵瞏聲. The graph 还 is documented as a graphic variant of 還 and is used as its simplified form. A separate dictionary entry associates a graph 还 with 不 and other readings, but does not establish a connection to this variant.

uncertainties.text: The relationship between the reported early forms and the later 辵/瞏 construction is unresolved. The separately recorded 不-associated graph 还 is not established as part of the modern variant’s history.
The received analysis identifies 瞏 as the sound element and a reported Old Chinese comparison exists, but the component’s identity and the sound fit are not independently verified.

senses.text: The received dictionary glosses 還 as 復, “return/repeat,” and cited classical material records “return.” Exact dates for the cited works and artifacts are not given here.

senses.period: bronze and classical attestations; exact dates unresolved
senses.text: 還 is attested with the sense “go around” or “circle.” Its chronological relation to “return” is not established.
A classical citation uses 還 to mean “immediately.” Its relation to “return” or other senses is not established.

senses.period: Tang citations and later uses; exact chronology unresolved
senses.text: Adverbial uses include “still” and “yet”; a Tang citation has the sense “still/again.” No dated chain connects these uses to “return.”

senses.period: later cited uses; exact chronology unresolved
senses.text: Cited uses include “also,” “more,” and “besides.” Their individual chronology and any path from “return” are not established.

limitations.text: The cited sources document several senses but do not establish a dated sequence or semantic bridges from “return” to “still,” “yet,” “also,” “more,” or “immediately.”

In cited manuscript passages, 還 is proposed as a sound-based spelling for 懷 and 環: the written sign was reused for other words thought to have sounded alike or similarly. The cited material supplies no pronunciation comparisons to demonstrate either match, so these spellings do not show meanings developing from “return.”

overview.text: 还 is the simplified form of 還, whose documented meaning includes “return; go back.” Later 還 combines a movement-related element with a sound element. Modern 还 also means “still” and “yet”; how these senses relate to “return” is unclear.

不 appears in modern 还, but is not established as part of the older 還 construction.
瞏 is identified as a sound element in 還; a reported comparison proposes a sound relationship but does not independently verify its fit.

takeaway.text: The visible 不 in 还 does not establish a sound role in the older construction of 還.
